coach.title: Personal AI Coach

welcome.0: Let's sharpen your Connect Four tactics.

onboardingMission.greeting: Hi, I'm your coach. Here's how we'll make you dangerous at Connect Four.

coach.emptyQueue: No positions in queue — keep training to build your personal curriculum.

prompt.0: You can win right now — find the column.
prompt.1: There's an immediate winning move on the board. Can you spot it?
prompt.2: One move ends the game in your favor. Where do you play?

hint.0: Look for a row where you're one move from four in a row.
hint.1: Check each of your existing groups of three — is any of them one away from connecting?

optimal.0: Nice — you spotted the winning move.

suboptimal.0: Close — there was a faster win available.

prompt.0: Your opponent is about to win — stop them.
prompt.1: There's a forced block you must make. Find it.
prompt.2: One column is the only safe move. Which is it?

hint.0: Look for a row where your opponent is one move from four in a row.
hint.1: Check each of your opponent's groups of three — is any of them one away from connecting?

optimal.0: Well defended — you blocked the threat.

suboptimal.0: You blocked, but there was a cleaner defensive move.

blunder.0: That leaves your opponent's winning threat wide open.

prompt.0: Find the move that creates two winning threats at once.
prompt.1: One column sets up two simultaneous threats your opponent can't both stop.
prompt.2: Look for a fork — a move that threatens in two directions.

hint.0: Think about moves that add to two different groups at once.
hint.1: A double threat wins because your opponent can only block one.

optimal.0: Perfect — you created the double threat.

suboptimal.0: Good move, but a different column creates two threats at once.

blunder.0: That misses the chance to create two simultaneous threats.

prompt.0: As Gray, you can secure a draw — find the Claimeven move.
prompt.1: Gray has a drawing strategy here. Which column keeps it alive?
prompt.2: Use Claimeven: Gray plays below every Green even-row threat.

hint.0: Look for an even row where Green has a threat — Gray should mirror below it.
hint.1: Claimeven works by ensuring Gray always gets the square directly below Green's even-row threats.

optimal.0: Exactly — that's the Claimeven move that secures the draw.

suboptimal.0: You're still in the draw zone, but the Claimeven key column was stronger.

blunder.0: That column gives up Gray's Claimeven drawing advantage.

prompt.0: A Z-threat gives you unstoppable parity control — find it.
prompt.1: Use the Z-threat pattern to guarantee you get the winning odd-row square.
prompt.2: One column sets up Z-threat parity so your opponent can't stop you.

hint.0: Look for a column where your odd-row threat can't be claimed by your opponent.
hint.1: Z-threats work by creating a parity chain your opponent is forced to follow.

optimal.0: Spot on — you activated the Z-threat.

suboptimal.0: Reasonable move, but the Z-threat column creates stronger parity control.

blunder.0: That move hands away your Z-threat parity advantage.

prompt.0: Green has two threat moves. One lands on an odd row (Green's home row) — that's the winner. Which column do you choose?
prompt.1: Both moves create threats, but one lands on an odd row — Green's natural parity. That's the move that gives Green lasting control. Play it.

hint.0: One of the threat moves lands on an odd row. Odd rows belong to Green — that's the correct target.

optimal.0: Correct! The odd-row threat gives Green parity control — it can't be neutralised by Gray's claimeven strategy.
optimal.1: Exactly right. Playing to the odd row aligns with Green's natural parity advantage.

suboptimal.0: That move creates a threat, but it lands on an even row — Gray's parity. The odd-row threat in the other column is stronger.

blunder.0: That column doesn't create a threat at all. Look for the moves that create an immediate winning window.

prompt.0: Mark every column that would hand your opponent an immediate win.
prompt.1: Which columns are forbidden? Tag them all before submitting.
prompt.2: Find every column where you would lose instantly — mark them all.

hint.0: Look for columns where your opponent already has three in a row — playing there hands them a win.
hint.1: Check each column: would your opponent win immediately if you played there?

optimal.0: Perfect — you identified every forbidden column.

suboptimal.0: You found some but missed {{missed}} forbidden column(s).

blunder.0: You tagged a safe column — that counts as a mistake.
blunder.1: At least one of your tagged columns was safe to play.

prompt.0: Force the win — play the line that leaves your opponent no escape.
prompt.1: There's a forcing sequence here. Play it move by move.
prompt.2: Every move must threaten your opponent. Find the forcing line.

optimal.0: You forced the win — well played.
optimal.1: Perfect sequence — your opponent had no escape.

blunder.0: That move breaks the forcing line.
blunder.1: The sequence fails here — your opponent can escape.

prompt.0: Spot the Figure-7 pattern — find the move that creates two unstoppable threats.
prompt.1: An L-shaped pattern is forming. Play the key cell to complete it.
prompt.2: The Figure-7 trap is on the board. One move creates two threats.

hint.0: Look for an L-shaped cluster of 4 discs — the fifth piece locks in two threats.
hint.1: Figure 7 creates two threats the opponent can't both block.

optimal.0: Figure-7 trap complete — your opponent cannot block both threats.
optimal.1: That completes the Figure-7 pattern. Two unstoppable threats.
optimal.2: Perfect — the L-shape locks in. Your opponent is trapped.
optimal.3: Exactly the right cell — the opponent can block one threat but not both.

suboptimal.0: Good move, but completing the Figure-7 pattern was stronger.
suboptimal.1: Close — the Figure-7 key cell creates two threats at once.
suboptimal.2: Solid play, but the Figure-7 completion was the decisive move here.

blunder.0: That misses the Figure-7 trap. Look for the L-shaped pattern.
blunder.1: Wrong cell — the Figure-7 pattern needs one specific completing piece.
blunder.2: That doesn't create the double threat. Find the key cell of the Figure-7.
blunder.3: You missed the Figure-7. Scan for an L-shape of 4 discs.

prompt.0: The J-Shape creates three winning directions — find the key cell.
prompt.1: An L-shaped cluster of 4 discs — complete it to create triple threats.
prompt.2: Find the J-Shape completing cell. Your opponent can't block all three threats.

hint.0: The J-Shape is an L-cluster. The completing cell unlocks three threat directions.
hint.1: Look for 4 discs in an L — the fifth piece creates threats vertically, horizontally, and diagonally.

optimal.0: J-Shape complete — three threat directions. Unblockable!
optimal.1: That locks in the J-Shape. Your opponent can block one, maybe two — not all three.
optimal.2: Perfect — vertical, horizontal, and diagonal threats. Game over.
optimal.3: Exactly — the triple threat from the J-Shape is unstoppable.

suboptimal.0: Good, but completing the J-Shape gives you three unblockable threats.
suboptimal.1: Solid move, but the J-Shape completing cell was the decisive play.
suboptimal.2: Not bad — the J-Shape cell creates threats in three directions at once.

blunder.0: That doesn't complete the J-Shape. Look for the L-cluster and its key cell.
blunder.1: Wrong cell — the J-Shape needs one specific completing piece.
blunder.2: You missed the J-Shape. The L-cluster of 4 discs is the clue.
blunder.3: That skips the triple threat. Find the J-Shape completing cell.

prompt.0: Two threats, same column — the upper one wins. Find the overcut.
prompt.1: The overcut beats the undercut. Same parity, upper threat wins.
prompt.2: Play above your opponent's threat to neutralize it — find the overcut.

hint.0: Look for an upper threat that beats a lower one — same parity row.
hint.1: The overcut works when both threats share the same parity.

optimal.0: Perfect overcut — the upper threat neutralizes the lower one.
optimal.1: Same parity advantage — your upper threat wins the column.
optimal.2: Clean overcut. Your opponent's lower threat can't reach first.
optimal.3: Exactly — playing above the threat gives you the advantage.

suboptimal.0: Good move, but the overcut column gave you a stronger position.
suboptimal.1: Close — there was a column where an upper threat beats a lower one.
suboptimal.2: Not bad, but the overcut opportunity was more decisive.

blunder.0: That column doesn't exploit the overcut — your opponent's threat survives.
blunder.1: You missed the overcut. The upper threat wins when parity is the same.
blunder.2: Wrong column — look for same-parity threats where upper beats lower.
blunder.3: That skips the overcut advantage. Same parity, upper threat wins.

prompt.0: Two threats in the same column — the lower one wins. Find the undercut.
prompt.1: An undercut is waiting — identify the column where a lower threat kills an upper one.
prompt.2: Gravity works in your favor here. Find the undercut move.

hint.0: Look for a column with threats at two different rows — the lower one wins.
hint.1: Same column, opposite parity rows — the undercut is a gravity exploit.

optimal.0: That undercut neutralizes the upper threat perfectly.
optimal.1: Gravity does the work — the lower threat wins the column.
optimal.2: Clean undercut. Your opponent's upper threat is dead.
optimal.3: Exactly right — same column, lower threat kills the upper one.

suboptimal.0: Good thinking, but the undercut column was the killing move here.
suboptimal.1: Close — there was a column where a lower threat neutralizes an upper one.
suboptimal.2: Not bad, but you missed the undercut opportunity.

blunder.0: That plays into the wrong parity — the undercut was elsewhere.
blunder.1: You missed the undercut column. The lower threat wins.
blunder.2: Wrong column — your opponent's threat is still alive.
blunder.3: That doesn't exploit the gravity advantage. Look again.

optimal.18: That's how you stay in control.

suboptimal.0: Not bad, but there was a sharper move.
suboptimal.1: You're close — try to find the stronger option.
suboptimal.2: Reasonable, but not the best here.

blunder.0: Hmm, not the strongest move there.
blunder.2: That one's tricky — check the hint if you're stuck.
blunder.3: That leaves a gap for your opponent.
blunder.5: Your opponent has a good answer to that.

claimeven.1: I'll take that even-row claim. Your threat is neutralized.

z_threat.1: I've secured the parity chain. You'd need an even number of moves to stop me.

odd_even_threat.0: Playing to the odd row — that's parity control on my side.
odd_even_threat.1: Odd-row threat in place. Even rows won't save you.

forced_win.0: I can force you to lose from here — let's see if you can find the escape.
forced_win.1: The path is forced — find the escape if you can.

figure_7.0: Figure-7 trap set — two threats you can't both stop.
figure_7.1: I've completed the Figure-7. Two threats incoming.

j_shape.0: J-Shape in place — I'm threatening in three directions now.
j_shape.1: Three simultaneous threats. You can block one, maybe two.

overcut.0: Overcut — my upper threat beats yours in this column.
overcut.1: Same parity, upper wins. Your lower threat is dead.

socratic.ask: I'm going to make a mistake here. See if you can punish it.
socratic.wrong1: Not quite — look for the right square. Try again.
socratic.hint: Look for an even square directly above one of my discs.

socratic.ask: You move first — where is the strongest opening move?
socratic.hint: Which column sits on the most possible four-in-a-row lines?
socratic.correct: Exactly — the centre column. It keeps the most winning paths alive.

socratic.ask: Gray just played column 2 again. What is Green's best reply?
socratic.hint: Which column sits directly above Gray's last disc?
socratic.correct: Exactly — play where they play. Answering directly above Gray's last disc keeps the imitation going.

socratic.ask: Green dominates the third row on the right, Gray has compensation on the fifth row on the left. Green to move — only one column wins. Which one?
socratic.hint: Look at Green's threats on the right flank. Which column completes them right now?
socratic.correct: Exactly — that column completes Green's third-row threat right now. Every other column throws the win away; this is Allen's 'only one move to win' Third-Row Gambit.
